prompt_text:
Assume the role of a cybersecurity threat intelligence annotation expert.
Extract named entities from the given text using ONLY the four categories specified here:
- Vulnerability: must be a literal CVE identifier in the form CVE-YYYY-NNNN (e.g., CVE-2021-44228). Known vulnerability names (such as "Log4Shell", "Snake", "EternalBlue") or non-CVE descriptions are NOT to be labeled as Vulnerabilities, even if they refer to a known flaw. Only exact CVE-YYYY-NNNN substrings are valid.
- Weakness: a specific CWE identifier (e.g., CWE-89) or fundamental flaw class.
- Configuration: a specific product, software, component, device, or CPE identifier that could be affected by vulnerabilities. Generic filenames, IP addresses, ports, or arbitrary strings that are not clearly identifiable affected products/components must NOT be tagged as Configuration (e.g., "comadmin.dat", "104.155.149[.]103", "443", "winds.exe" are excluded unless explicitly presented as a product/component name).
- AttackTechnique: a MITRE ATT&CK technique ID (e.g., T1190, T1090.002, T1078, TA0011) or explicitly named attack method. Each distinct ID occurrence must be its own entity containing only the exact ID substring (e.g., from "Valid Accounts (T1078, ICS T0859)" extract "T1078" and "T0859" separately, not the full phrase). Both sub-technique IDs (e.g., T1090.002) and parent technique IDs (e.g., T1090) are valid when explicitly stated. Only exact MITRE ATT&CK T-code or TA-code substrings qualify; do NOT tag software/tool IDs such as S0508, S1063, S1054 as AttackTechnique.

Rules:
1. All entity text MUST be an exact verbatim substring from the input text.
2. Provide 0-based start and end character offsets based on the input text. end is exclusive, so text[start:end] equals the entity text exactly.
3. For normalized_id, provide the canonical identifier if present (e.g., standard CVE ID, CWE-xxx, canonical CPE 2.3 URI for products, or T-code for ATT&CK); otherwise null.
4. Do not output repeated duplicate entries for the identical mention span.
5. Extract only entities that satisfy the strict definitions. Skip any span that does not clearly fit one of the four types per the rules.
6. For AttackTechnique, capture solely the exact ID token (e.g., "T1090.002", "T1078") as entity text, never the surrounding descriptive words.
7. Never infer or insert entities not present as exact substrings in the input text. Do not hallucinate configurations, products, vulnerability names, or technique IDs that are not explicitly written in the provided text.
8. Output ONLY the specified JSON schema fields per entity: id, text, type, start, end, normalized_id. Do not add fields beyond the specified schema (e.g., no "evidence", "notes", or other extra keys).

Reference Samples:
<example>
<text>
Attackers exploited CVE-2021-44228 in the Log4j component to gain initial access by exploiting a public-facing application (T1190).
</text>
<entities>

  {"id": "E2", "text": "Log4j", "type": "Configuration", "start": 42, "end": 47, "normalized_id": "cpe:2.3:a:apache:log4j:*:*:*:*:*:*:*:*"},
  {"id": "E3", "text": "T1190", "type": "AttackTechnique", "start": 124, "end": 129, "normalized_id": "T1190"}
]
</entities>
</example>

</entities>
</example>

A TTP associated with this actor is the use of residential proxies (T1090.002). The SVR use password spraying (T1110) and valid accounts (T1078).
</text>

  {"id": "E2", "text": "T1110", "type": "AttackTechnique", "start": 102, "end": 107, "normalized_id": "T1110"},

Assume the role of a cyber threat intelligence annotation expert.
Extract named entities from the given text using ONLY the following four types:
- Vulnerability: a specific CVE identifier (e.g., CVE-YYYY-NNNN).
- Weakness: a specific CWE identifier (e.g., CWE-89) OR a widely recognized flaw class name explicitly stated as a vulnerability category (e.g., "server-side request forgery", "SQL injection"). Only extract Weakness entities if (a) a CWE-xxx identifier appears verbatim in the text, or (b) a widely recognized flaw type name is explicitly stated as a vulnerability class. Do NOT infer, guess, or normalize descriptive vulnerability phrases (such as "improper authentication", "missing authentication check", "buffer overflow condition") into Weakness entities unless they are established flaw category names. If no CWE ID or explicit recognized flaw class is present, output no Weakness entities.
- Configuration: an actual product, software, component, device, or CPE identifier that may be impacted by vulnerabilities.
- AttackTechnique: a MITRE ATT&CK technique ID (e.g., T1190, T1190.002, TA0011) or clearly named attack method.

Rules:
1. The entity text must be copied verbatim as a substring from the source text.
2. Provide 0-based start and end character offsets based on the input text. End is exclusive so that text[start:end] equals the entity text precisely.
3. For normalized_id, supply the canonical identifier when possible (e.g., official CVE ID, CWE-xxx, canonical CPE 2.3 URI for products, or T-code for ATT&CK); if not available, use null.
4. Avoid repeating the same mention span (identical text, start, and end) as duplicate entries.
5. AttackTechnique IDs: Capture EVERY distinct explicit MITRE ATT&CK identifier string (covering technique IDs like T1190, sub-technique IDs like T1190.002, tactic IDs like TA0011, and ICS technique IDs like T0859) as an INDIVIDUAL entity. The entity text should be solely the ID token (e.g., "T1090", "T1090.002", "T1078", "T0859", "TA0011"), not the accompanying description (e.g., NOT "Valid Accounts (T1078, ICS T0859)"). Do NOT extract software/tool names (e.g., S0508, S1063, S0357) as AttackTechnique entities; only extract MITRE ATT&CK T-code or TA-code identifiers.
6. Parent/child or overlapping technique IDs: When both a parent ID and a sub-technique ID appear explicitly and overlap (e.g., "T1090.002" includes "T1090"), extract EACH distinct ID string as a separate entity with its own offsets, even if spans overlap. For instance: from "(T1090.002)" extract "T1090" (start at T, end after T1090) and "T1090.002" (start at T, end after 002) as two entities.
7. Do not classify IP addresses, file names, tool names, ports, or similar as Configuration unless they are explicitly a product, software, component, device, or CPE identifier vulnerable to exploits. Generic indicators (e.g., 104.155.149[.]103, winds.exe, 443) are NOT Configuration entities. Extract only the specific product/software/component name (e.g., "FortiOS", "SAP NetWeaver"), not version strings or descriptive phrases appended to it, unless the version is part of the official product name in text.
8. If no entities of the permitted types exist, output an empty list.
